items.followUp: Differentiate between organic and inorganic compounds in cells, giving one example of each.

rubric.why: Micromolecules are small molecules with low molecular mass; glucose, amino acids and water are examples.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying micromolecules as small or low-molecular-mass molecules and giving a suitable example.

rubric.why: Macromolecules are large molecules with high molecular mass; proteins, starch, nucleic acids and polysaccharides are examples.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying macromolecules as large or high-molecular-mass molecules and giving a suitable example.

modelAnswer: Micromolecules are small molecules with low molecular mass, for example glucose or amino acids.
Macromolecules are large molecules with high molecular mass, for example proteins or starch.

items.followUp: Define exocytosis and describe how it occurs.

rubric.why: Endocytosis takes substances into the cell when the plasma membrane surrounds them and forms a vesicle.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing uptake into the cell by membrane enclosure or vesicle formation.

rubric.why: The two types are phagocytosis, which takes in solid particles, and pinocytosis, which takes in liquids.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming both types and correctly identifying phagocytosis with solids and pinocytosis with liquids.

modelAnswer: Endocytosis is the process by which a cell takes substances in when its plasma membrane surrounds them and forms a vesicle.
Phagocytosis, or cell eating, is the uptake of solid particles.
Pinocytosis, or cell drinking, is the uptake of liquids.
